bull.b: Cadence's very high gross margins and strong operating profitability are durable advantages in EDA: they reflect pricing power, scalable software economics, and the ability to invest in R&D and partnerships without eroding core margins, supporting long-term cash generation and competitive moat.

bull.t: Robust free cash flow and buyback capacity
bull.b: Consistent, high free cash flow gives Cadence durable financial flexibility: it funds sustained R&D, strategic integrations and share repurchases, reduces dependence on external financing for growth initiatives, and provides a cushion versus cyclical swings in customer R&D spend.

bull.t: Leadership in EDA/IP with strategic foundry partnerships
bull.b: Broad product breadth (EDA, IP, SDA) plus deep foundry and OEM engagements create multi-year demand visibility and high switching costs. Record backlog and expanding IP traction support durable wallet share gains and long-term TAM expansion, including new agentic-AI workflows.

bear.b: The meaningful increase in leverage reduces financial flexibility and raises refinancing and interest-rate sensitivity. If growth or cash flow weakens, higher debt levels could constrain strategic options, slow buybacks, or force more conservative capital allocation.

bear.t: Decelerating revenue growth vs prior years
bear.b: A material slowdown in underlying revenue growth compresses the runway for margin expansion and makes organic scaling harder. Management may need to increase investment, M&A or pricing actions, raising execution risk and putting pressure on sustaining prior profitability levels.

bear.t: Sensitivity to export controls / regulatory shifts
bear.b: Geopolitical and export-control changes can structurally constrain addressable markets and partner integrations. Such regulatory shifts could delay shipments, restrict customer engagements, and materially affect backlog monetization and long-term revenue visibility.
